comment: THE DERIVED-CLAIMS REGISTRY — discharges CHECK-DEBT D2.8 (doctrine B.7).
B.7: 'One harness parses a constant out of the bible and asserts the running module's
constants equal what the specification says. Changing the specification without changing
the code is RED, and changing the code without changing the specification is also RED.'
THIS FILE STORES NO EXPECTED VALUES. There is not one integer in it. A claim is a set of
SOURCES that must agree; each source is a command that prints an integer it computed from
the tree at run time. Storing the number here would reproduce, inside the instrument built
to catch it, the exact defect the instrument exists to catch (arc_017 s0a records that
happening in the arc brief itself).
ROLES. 'derived' = computed from ground truth (the frozen spec, the registry, the real
collector). 'stated' = a number a document, config, or code file asserts. A claim needs at
least two sources; a lone number is unchecked by construction.
restatement_scans: OPTIONAL patterns naming places where this number has historically been
written down in prose. EVERY match must equal the agreed value; ZERO matches is the better
outcome and is reported as such — deleting a restatement is the doctrine-correct repair,
syncing it is only the second-best one.
SCOPE, v1: numeric claims only. Prose facts are out of scope and must not be smuggled in as
a count of words that happen to match.
EVIDENCE BASE — TEN measured instances of derive-never-restate failing in THIS project:
1. CHECK-DEBT series hand-counted wrong (ARC 010 row).
2. CHECK-DEBT series hand-counted wrong AGAIN (ARC 011 row) — same author, same table.
3. The 10-minute feed delay sat uncomputed inside ARC 010's own banked output.
4. avg_price unit mismatch: per-unit vs notional, both spellings live, last writer won.
5. The ARC 016 brief cited D2.8 as the vacuous-pass class; D2.8 is the restatement class.
6. The CHECK-DEBT series table silently skipped ARC 014 and ARC 015 entirely.
7. '19 verbs/events' survived three arcs because TWO unrelated derivations both land on 19
— 19 markdown BULLETS across both libraries, and 8+7+4 = 19 ARC 014 findings. By
IDENTIFIER broker-order is 16. A coincidence is what made a wrong number look checked.
8. The ARC 017 brief's own s7 anchored the expected check count while s6 asked for it to be
derived; caught before execution and recorded in s0a.
9. The s7 derivation command itself: re.findall('check_[a-z0-9_]+') over verify.py. The path
was wrong, and against the corrected path it returns 1 — verify.py holds no check names
at all. A derivation that cannot express the number it claims to derive.
10. .pre-commit-config.yaml restated '126 tests' in TWO comments while the real collected
count was 159 — the first instance found inside a GATE'S OWN CONFIGURATION rather than a
document. ARC 017 removed the restatements rather than syncing them, which is why the
pytest claim below carries restatement_scans that should now match ZERO times.
NOT REGISTERED, DELIBERATELY: the string '19 verbs/events - 8 CLEAN, 7 FRICTION, 4 GAP'.
It is not a literal anywhere in this tree; it is what summarise() PRINTS from FINDINGS, and
its defect is a mislabel (19 findings presented as 19 verbs/events), not a stale integer.
Registering the string would pin the gate to a number ARC 017 has established is wrong.
Claim arc014_broker_order_classification registers the RE-DERIVED total instead.

placeholders.{self}: checks/check_derived_claims.py, re-entered as a probe runner

claims.property: how many checks are registered, counted two ways that cannot share a bug
note: The two answers are independent: registry.json is what verify.py RUNS, the glob is what
is on DISK. They diverge exactly when a check is written and never registered (invisible
to every runner) or registered and deleted (CANNOT_MEASURE at run time). Either is a real
defect and neither is visible from one side alone.
DO NOT reintroduce the naive derivation re.findall('check_[a-z0-9_]+') over verify.py:
verify.py contains no check names — it loads a manifest — and that expression returns 1.

claims.property: how many tests the suite really collects

restatement_scans.note: the pytest-affected hook's live claim; removed by ARC 017
the B101 comment's wrapped '126\n tests, ~100 sites'; removed by ARC 017

note: source_ast counts `def test_*` and multiplies by each parametrize case list, so it is a
genuinely different mechanism from pytest's collector rather than the same walk twice.
They diverge when the collector stops seeing files it should see — a testpaths change, a
conftest that deselects, a module that fails to import. That is CHECK-DEBT D2.12's
property ('a suite that silently skips a gate reports GREEN') measured from outside the
suite. A dated historical measurement in prose ('ARC 017 derived 159 tests') is NOT
matched by the scans above and is deliberately out of scope: history is append-only.
MEASURED ARC 017: both scans now match ZERO times. ARC 017 DELETED the two live '126'
restatements rather than syncing them to 159, which is the doctrine-correct repair, so
these patterns are now a tripwire against reintroduction rather than a live comparison.
KNOWN FRAGILITY, stated so it is not discovered as a surprise: .pre-commit-config.yaml
still QUOTES the removed text as history ('It used to read "126 tests"', 'are now 126').
Those quotations are line-wrapped and the patterns do not reach them. Re-wrapping that
comment onto one line would make the first pattern match a historical quotation and turn
this claim red for the wrong reason. If that happens the repair is to the pattern.

claims.property: how many venv pins exist, per the file and per its only validated reader
note: install.sh consumes `--print-pins`, not the JSON. If load_pins ever drops a pin on the
floor — a token-guard rejection, a key collision after lower-casing — the file and the
shell-visible list disagree and install.sh silently installs fewer packages than pinned.

claims.property: how many debts are open, counted from the rows vs what the series table says
note: Evidence instances 1, 2 and 6. The stated source reads the LAST series row by position,
never by arc name — anchoring to 'ARC 016' would be the stale literal anchor this gate
exists to remove, and would go stale the next time a row is appended. A row that is never
appended still fails: the previous row's number will not match the new count.

claims.property: how many broker-order verbs+events section 2A defines, spec vs seam code
note: THE B.7 PAIR. The frozen spec is the authority and may never be edited; broker_seam.py's
ORDER_PORT_VERBS + ORDER_EVENTS is the code restating it. Adding a verb to the seam
without the spec is RED; the spec growing one the seam has not implemented is RED.
COUNTED BY IDENTIFIER, NOT BY BULLET. 'connect() / disconnect()' is ONE markdown bullet
and TWO verbs. Counting bullets gives 15 here and 19 across both libraries, which is
evidence instance 7 — the number that survived three arcs.

claims.property: ARC 014's CLEAN/FRICTION/GAP mapping re-derived against the real 16-element roster
note: THREE derivations, not two, and that is the point. Evidence instance 7 survived because
TWO unrelated derivations coincided on 19; a third breaks a coincidence that a second
cannot. Sources 2 and 3 also make a real assertion beyond arithmetic: source 2 says every
section 2A broker-order element is graded by ARC 014, so a NEW seam element with no
finding reddens this claim rather than passing unnoticed.
The grade breakdown itself is derived and printed to stderr by both probes on every run;
it is NOT stored here, because storing it would anchor the gate to today's grades.

claims.property: every element the seam declares is either in section 2A or a FLAGGED Nix addition
note: The frozen spec cannot be edited, so the seam legitimately declares more than section 2A
does — feed_lag() is the precedent, flagged 'Nix addition' in its own docstring. This
claim makes the FLAG load-bearing rather than decorative: an element the seam declares
that section 2A does not define and whose docstring does not name it as an addition is
counted by the code side and not by the spec side, and the two disagree. That is the
difference between an extension and a drift, made mechanical.

claims.property: how many .py files the ban gate believes it covers, derived from the tree vs from its stated anchor
note: ARC 018, CHECK-DEBT D2.15. The file set a gate believes it covers is exactly the kind of
number that goes stale silently — debug.md §8 failure mode #14, the scope set by a list a
person edits.
THE TWO SOURCES ARE INDEPENDENT IN MECHANISM. `gate_derived_scope` asks the gate itself for
the scope it will actually read, and that scope is derived FROM FILE CONTENT: a directory
is in scope because some module in it declares ORDER_PORT_VERBS or defines a class carrying
at least PORT_QUORUM roster verbs as methods. `stated_anchor_dirs` globs the PATH the gate's
ORDER_PATH_DIRS constant names — read out of the gate by AST rather than retyped here, so
this probe is not itself a restatement.
WHAT A DISAGREEMENT MEANS, and it is not a bug in either side: the order path has acquired a
second home, or has moved. The gate SELF-HEALS — the new home joins its scan the moment the
file is written, which is D2.15's actual requirement — and this claim makes that change
VISIBLE rather than silent, so a human confirms the new home and updates the anchor. A gate
whose scope grows without anyone noticing is the same defect one direction over.
MEASURED ARC 018: the second-home case was planted (an adapter at scripts/limiter/ defining
four roster verbs) and the gate's scope went 4 files / 1 dir -> 5 files / 2 dirs, naming a
retry shape inside the plant. Restored, the scope returned to 4 / 1.
RESIDUAL, stated so it is not discovered as a surprise: a module that CALLS the order port
without DECLARING it — the future Limiter — is in neither source. §7.12 condition 4 beside
the gate carries the full statement.

claims.property: broker-order ELEMENT COVERAGE (breadth) under scheme `sec2a-element-v1`, both terms re-derived

restatement_scans.note: the CANONICAL written form of this scheme's level AFTER the ARC 020 rename. Zero matches is the preferred outcome; the pattern is a tripwire that goes live the moment anyone writes the level down in prose. It deliberately does NOT match a per-arc DELTA — a delta and a level are different quantities over the same denominator, and matching both would redden this claim for the wrong reason. Only downloads/RESULTS.md is scanned, because it is overwritten every arc and is therefore always current; sessions/SESSION.md and the CHECK-DEBT series table are APPEND-ONLY history, and a dated historical figure there is correct forever and must never be compared against today's derivation.

THE PRE-RENAME CANONICAL FORM, kept as a tripwire rather than deleted. ARC 020 renamed the claim but did NOT change the scheme or the derivation, so a document still written in the old form is stating this same quantity and must still state it correctly. Measured ARC 018 and again ARC 020: zero matches. If a future arc confirms the old spelling is gone from every live document, deleting this pattern is the doctrine-correct repair; syncing it would be the second-best one.

note: RENAMED ARC 020 (C1, operator ruling) from `broker_order_percent_sec2a_element_v1`. THE
RENAME IS A FRAMING CORRECTION, NOT A NEW MEASUREMENT — the scheme identifier, both probes
and the cross-derivation are unchanged, and the value is continuous across the rename.
WHY IT WAS RENAMED. The old name said 'percent' and the number read as completeness. It is
not completeness; it is BREADTH, and it is blind to depth. ARC 019 is the measured instance:
an arc that closed four defects, discovered five more, corrected a banked performance figure
fivefold and produced the module's first Tier-3 traversal registered as ZERO MOVEMENT under
this scheme — correctly, because it added no elements. The name now carries the limitation.
'PERCENT MOVED' IS RETIRED AS A FRAMING FOR THIS SCHEME. A change in this level is a change
in ELEMENT COVERAGE and is named as such; it is never presented as how far the module moved.
The depth companion is the separate claim `broker_order_open_debt_rows`, which is a COUNT and
is deliberately not a percent.
NO CONFIDENCE DIMENSION WAS INVENTED, and that is a decision rather than an omission. A
per-element confidence score is a hand-maintained rubric, which is the stale-anchor class
this whole registry exists to remove.
THE SCHEME. `sec2a-element-v1`. coverage(level) = 100 * |broker-order elements graded
CLEAN| / |broker-order roster|, the roster being the frozen spec's section 2A set BY
IDENTIFIER. The identifier is registered ALONGSIDE the
value — it is carried in this claim's id and it is printed by both probes on every run — so a
future change of scheme appears as a new claim id rather than as a silent discontinuity in a
series that kept its name.
THE OTHER NUMBER. A prior architect estimate used a readiness-weighted decomposition and
produced ~42% for the same module. It is NOT comparable to this scheme and both called
themselves 'broker-order percent' — the 19-vs-16 shape recurring inside the progress number.
MEASURED ARC 018: `grep -rIn '42%'` over the whole tree, `git log --all -S'42%'` over the
whole history, and an XML extraction over both .docx files return NOTHING except this note.
The ~42% figure appears in exactly ONE place in this project: the ARC 018 brief itself,
downloads/arc_018_runtime_gate_truth.md, which is a task document and not a banked
artifact. It has never been in the repository, in any banked result, or in any commit. So
there was no restatement to delete; the retirement is a RULE, not a repair, and the rule
is: readiness commentary continues as
PROSE and is never expressed as a percent, so two incomparable numbers cannot both claim the
name again. This note is the only place the string exists, and it exists here as a record
that the search was run rather than as a value anyone should reuse.
HOW THE SOURCES ARE INDEPENDENT, AND WHERE THEY ARE NOT — stated because §7.12 condition 3
requires it and because overstating it would be the defect this file exists to catch. The
DENOMINATORS are genuinely independent: one is a markdown parse of the frozen spec's §2A
bullets by identifier, the other is a Python AST read of broker_seam.py's ORDER_PORT_VERBS +
ORDER_EVENTS. They diverge whenever the seam drifts from the spec. The NUMERATORS share a
mechanism — both read ARC 014's FINDINGS out of ibkr_mapping.py — so a defect in FINDINGS
itself would move both sides together. That residual is why this claim is a THIRD assertion
on top of spec_2a_broker_order_elements and arc014_broker_order_classification rather than a
replacement for either: those two already pin the roster and the grade tally from three
directions.
WHAT THIS CLAIM DOES NOT FIX, and ARC 018 found it rather than reconciling toward the brief:
ARC 017 reported broker-order at ~13%, and that number is 2/16 where 16 is the machine-
derived roster size and 2 is an ARC-LOCAL HAND COUNT of defects closed. The DENOMINATOR was
derivable; the NUMERATOR was not, and no gate can make an arc's own count of what it closed
machine-derivable. What is registered here is the reproducible part — the denominator and
the level — so a future delta is at least stated over a denominator that cannot drift.
ARC 020 ADDS THE OTHER HALF OF THAT SENTENCE. A delta over a denominator that cannot drift
is still a delta in BREADTH. It was never the module's progress, and the ARC 019 measurement
above is the proof. That is what the rename fixes and what `broker_order_open_debt_rows`
exists to stand beside.

claims.property: how many OPEN ledger rows are scoped to broker-order — A COUNT, NEVER A PERCENT
note: ARC 020 / C2 — THE DEPTH COMPANION TO `broker_order_element_coverage_v1`.
WHY IT EXISTS. Element coverage is breadth and cannot see the work. It does not move when a
defect inside an already-CLEAN element is found and it does not move when one is fixed, so
ARC 019 — four defects closed, five discovered, the module's first Tier-3 traversal — scored
zero. This number moves in both of those directions: it RISES when a traversal finds defects
and FALLS when they are paid. It is fully derivable from the ledger and it needs no rubric,
which is precisely why it was chosen over a confidence score.
IT MUST NEVER BE EXPRESSED AS A PERCENT. THIS IS THE REASON, REGISTERED BESIDE THE CLAIM SO
A FUTURE READER CANNOT RE-DERIVE ONE. Making a percent of it requires a denominator, and the
only honest denominator is the total number of outstanding obligations this module has —
which is the same quantity as 'how much do we trust this module', and is unknowable. That is
NAMED GAP 5 exactly: condition 7 of the standing question in check_derived_claims.py states
that this instrument proves every REGISTERED number right and cannot prove the registry
covers the numbers that matter, so the denominator would be the size of a set nobody can
enumerate. A percent over an unknowable denominator is a confidence score wearing arithmetic
— the very rubric the C1 rename removed — and it would read as completeness for the second
time in the same module. The count is a FLOOR on outstanding broker-order obligations. It is
never a fraction of them.
THE MODULE-SCOPING RULE, stated so it can be argued with rather than inferred:
A row is BROKER-ORDER SCOPED iff it is OPEN — by the ledger's own bold-span rule, the same
regex `check_debt_open_items` uses — AND its row text names at least one order-path
artefact, being either (i) the basename of a Python module that exists under the order
path, or (ii) a broker-order roster identifier, matched on word boundaries.
NOTHING IN THE RULE IS TYPED. The order path is read by AST out of check_order_path_bans.py's
ORDER_PATH_DIRS anchor — the same non-restating technique order_path_scope_files uses — and
the basenames come off the disk.
HOW THE SOURCES ARE INDEPENDENT, AND WHERE THEY ARE NOT — stated because condition 3 of the
standing question requires it and because overstating it is the defect this file exists to
catch. INDEPENDENT: the roster half of the vocabulary. One side parses the frozen spec's
broker-order bullets by identifier; the other AST-reads broker_seam.py's ORDER_PORT_VERBS +
ORDER_EVENTS. That is the derive-never-restate pair, and the sources diverge exactly when the
seam drifts from the spec by NAME — which is a stronger assertion than
spec_2a_broker_order_elements makes, since that claim compares COUNTS and two rosters can
agree on 16 while disagreeing on which 16.
NOT INDEPENDENT, AND SAID PLAINLY: the ledger walk, the open-row rule and the module-basename
half of the vocabulary are SHARED by both sources. A defect in any of those three moves both
sides together and this claim would not see it. Two of the three are already asserted
elsewhere — the open-row rule by check_debt_open_items against the series table, the module
set by order_path_scope_files against the gate's content-derived scope — so this claim is a
third assertion layered on those, not a replacement for either.
WHAT IS AMBIGUOUS. Mechanical attribution is not the same as correct attribution, and the
rule's misses are named here rather than discovered later:
a. APPARATUS-ABOUT-THE-MODULE versus DEFECT-IN-THE-MODULE. Two of the selected rows are not
defects in the order path at all: D2.14 is a residual in the GATE that scans the order
path, and D3.8 is a test instrument that happens to live in a seam module. Both are
genuine outstanding broker-order obligations and both are counted. Whether 'scoped to
broker-order' means defects IN the code or obligations ABOUT it is a judgment; the rule
does not make it, it counts both, and this paragraph is the disclosure.
b. IT UNDER-COUNTS ROWS THAT TALK ABOUT THE MODULE WITHOUT NAMING ANYTHING IN IT. D1.11 is
deferred until 'broker-order code exists and can host the probe' and names no artefact, so
it is not selected — correct by the rule, arguably wrong in substance.
c. THE RULE READS PROSE. Rewording a row to drop the verb name silently removes it from the
count. That is failure mode #14 one level down — a scope set by text a person edits — and
the only mitigation is that every selected row id is printed on every run.
d. A ROW IS NOT A DEFECT. D1.24 lists five observed symptoms of one repair; D1.27 holds two
separate specification gaps. The claim counts the ledger's unit of account, which is the
row. Hence FLOOR, not census.
e. THE TWO ROSTERS CAN LEGITIMATELY DIVERGE. If the seam declares a broker-order element the
spec does not — a flagged Nix addition, the feed_lag() precedent — the seam-side
vocabulary gains a word the spec-side one lacks and the two sources can disagree. That is
the instrument working, not a defect in it, and it is the shape a future arc should expect
the first time an addition is declared on the order port.
NO restatement_scans ARE REGISTERED, DELIBERATELY. This number has never been written into a
document, and registering a pattern for a canonical prose form would invite one to be written
— in percent form, by the next person who wants a progress figure. If it is ever banked, the
form must be a bare count with the word 'rows' in it and a scan may be added then.
